title: Snelson and the Black press
summary: Snelson was dropped by the Pittsburgh Courier and Albert hired him; his travel stories ran in the Courier. Albert names the Courier and Chicago Defender and regrets losing his write-ups.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: Oh, I see. And Floyd Snelson was with you all the time?
No, no, he didn't handle any bands. The Pittsburgh Courier had dropped him as a writer, and I picked him up. Oh, I see.
So, he only was with you.

Right. And he, yeah. But, of course, he also would write stories that the Pittsburgh Courier would take on his travels, not only for me, but for other things that he would encounter, which kept him getting a little few bucks here and there. But, he drank it as fast as he got his checks.
But, he must have been a pretty good writer. Beautiful. He got publicity.
What about newspapers? Is there any other newspapers that you were in touch with, especially where Mike Luxembourg?

The Pittsburgh Courier was the biggest thing then, the Chicago Defender. I think most of those papers, the Pittsburgh Courier is still going, but I think the Chicago Defender has been deleted years ago.
Yeah, but there's a guy named Walter Allen is going through all, you know, the Baltimore for America.

Yeah. Well, most of the Negro papers had carried big stories. However, every white newspaper carried the stories when they came to town. Unfortunately, I didn't keep all of these write-ups, you know. You do have some scrapbooks, though, is it?
